subject: Post-demo: ops & incident SLA gaps for inference providers
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Meyer <dana.meyer@acmeenergy.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: ops & incident SLA gaps for inference providers

Hi Dana — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the operational questions you raised (especially around incident response and RCA cadence relative to hyperscalers).

Attachments included: redwood-sla-compare-vs-hyperscalers.pdf (high-level matrix) and a draft MAP workbook (MAP_Acme_Redwood.xlsx).

What we covered
- Demo highlights: unified runtime, automatic KV/prefix caching, multi-model routing, and dedicated pools for predictable throughput.
- Differentiators vs hyperscalers we called out: (a) transparent per-token economics + tooling to tune batching, (b) built-in fallbacks to cheaper model variants during capacity pressure, (c) consistent on-prem & hosted runtime with identical APIs.

Incident & escalation summary (short form)
- Support SLA: Standard P1 initial response: 4 hours; P2: 8 hours.
- Operational escalation: 24/7 on-call for Dedicated customers (escalation path: SE -> On-call Eng -> Ops Lead -> Head of Platform).
- RCA cadence: Preliminary incident note within 48 hours, draft RCA within 5 business days, final RCA within 7-10 business days for complex incidents.
- Credits: we publish line-item credit thresholds in the contract; for Dedicated customers we can discuss custom terms.

Proposed next tests (so the team can validate behavior vs a hyperscaler):
1) Fault-injection: simulate transient GPU preemption and observe automatic model fallbacks / rate limiting behavior.
2) Multi-region failover: cut east region and validate routing/fallback latency and cache warm-up.
3) Sustained load test: 10k concurrent inference tokens/minute to validate queuing and tail latencies under batching.
4) RCA exercise: ask our ops team to run an end-to-end RCA simulation (timing, data collected, draft cadence).

As next steps I suggest:
- You confirm which tests you want to run (1–3) and target windows for a short run (we can do a 30–60 minute window each).
- Kimberly will prepare a short runbook and contact list for on-call during tests.
- We’ll share the SLA comparison PDF and a draft MAP (attached).

If you want, we can fast-track an enterprise SLA addendum that shortens initial response windows and adds an expedited RCA option — Laura, copied, can escalate for contract review.

Thanks —
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez

Sergio — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few follow-ups from my side before I put this in front of procurement: 

1) For multi-region outages: how does Redwood handle live KV cache rehydration and cold-start latency if traffic is shifted to a different region? Hyperscalers tend to bias customers toward increasing replication which increases cost.
2) On RCA timing: 48 hours for a preliminary note is reasonable. For critical outages we need an initial call within 2 hours and a formal internal update within 24 hours. Is that something you can commit to for Dedicated or enterprise customers?
3) Can we see an example RCA (redacted) and a short runbook for the suggested fault-injection tests? Procurement will want to see run-time implications and potential credit terms tied to incident severity.

We’re most interested in tests 1 and 2 from your list; target week of Jul 27 for any disruptive tests.

Thanks —
Dana Meyer
Director, Product Ops — Acme Energy

Hi Dana — appreciate the prompt feedback. Short answers below and a few concrete commitments we can formalize in an enterprise addendum for Dedicated customers.

Multi-region cache / cold-start behavior
- We use a two-tier caching strategy: persistent KV layer (replicated asynchronously) + per-node in-memory prefix cache. On failover we aggressively rehydrate the prefix cache using a prioritized warm-path; typical additional latency is model-dependent but we target <200ms p50 for warm-up on recent models. We can run a focused test that tears down a region and measures the tail latencies you care about.

RCA and on-call timing
- Standard published: P1 initial response within 4 hours and preliminary incident note within 48 hours.
- For Dedicated enterprise customers we do offer a Fast-RCA add-on: initial call within 2 hours, interim update within 24 hours, and a draft RCA within 48 hours. We can include that as an optional SLA line in the contract (Laura, happy to run this up).

Examples / runbook
- I’ve shared a redacted sample RCA in the Drive link (see related_links). Kimberly will publish a concise runbook for the 2 fault-injection tests you requested (fault-injection + multi-region failover).

Proposed schedule
- Target week Jul 27 for disruptive tests: we’ll reserve a 2-hour window per test and provide an on-call contact + war room link.

Action items
- Dana: confirm you want tests 1 & 2 (fault-injection, multi-region) and preferred window(s) the week of Jul 27.
- Kimberly: prep runbook, list of telemetry we’ll collect, and on-call contacts.
- Laura: if we can confirm Fast-RCA add-on, please advise on approval path for a short-term exception on contract SLA language.

Thanks —
Sergio
